calls.head: Unstoppable force, meet immovable object
calls.body: The Stars are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Avalanche are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Stars’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots.
calls.call: The Stars’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Avalanche.

calls.body: The Stars are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Avalanche are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. We’ll side with the Avalanche’s defense.

calls.head: In close against from distance
calls.body: The Stars get in close, but the Avalanche mostly shoot from distance. Dallas is one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and Colorado is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Stars to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Colorado took away the good looks
surprises.body: Colorado is one of the league’s best at preventing dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Dallas’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 4.0% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.6% (about 6.2% against Colorado) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Hintz wins it in a shootout
paras: Colorado had a goal taken off for offside 1:55 in. Colorado had a goal taken off after a video review midway through the first. The Stars’ Oskar Bäck left in the first period and didn’t return. Gabriel Landeskog got the scoring started for the Avalanche early in the second. Miro Heiskanen tied it late in the second. Arttu Hyry gave the Stars the lead shorthanded early in the third. Brock Nelson made it 2-2 midway through the third. Those stung in a game that went to a shootout. Jason Robertson and Roope Hintz scored in the shootout for the Stars, and Hintz’s in the fourth round ended it.
The Avalanche had a little more of the play, but the Stars made their chances count. Casey DeSmith made 25 saves for the Stars, and Scott Wedgewood stopped 20 of 22.
The Stars killed all four Avalanche power plays. The Stars improved to 3-3-1, and the Avalanche dropped to 4-2-1.

items.text: Nathan MacKinnon’s eleven-game point streak against Dallas ended.
The Stars split the two-game set, a night after losing to the Avalanche.
Arttu Hyry scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 13.
The season series is even at 1-1.
